title: 0002 · Split #4471 and deduplicate by cause · support kb

support desk · kb
0002 · Split #4471 and deduplicate by cause

owner md-400
accepted
reviewed 2026-11-13 · 0 days ago

Decision and scope

Supersedes decision 0001: duplicates share a subject line. Keep that accepted record unchanged as history. Its accepted status does not make its old rule safe to follow.

This is the current desk rule for all products, not just sched-prod: merge reports only when evidence establishes the same underlying cause and fix. Similar subjects describe symptoms, not causes. Unknown causes stay separate and need investigation. Use each product’s configuration and reproduction evidence; do not apply the booking classifier to unrelated products.

The old triage rule and incident prose are unsafe as current instructions. The stale warning is a reason to check them, not proof by itself that they are wrong. The tenant-aware tables and examples below establish the contradiction.
What #4471 actually contains

The export has 427 rows and 412 unique reports merged into #4471. Its overlapping pages repeat 15 rows. Deduplicate by report ID before grouping or counting.

Parser ticket: 379 reports, across 11 tenants. The shared parser treats a day-first tenant's date as month-first. This is the majority cause that the original #4471 describes.
Booking-v3 hint ticket: 33 reports, across 3 tenants. Booking-v3 prints MM/DD/YYYY but its form interprets the input in the tenant's day-first locale. This needs its own fix, separate from the shared parser.

Intake guessed the wrong cause on 38 reports: 23 parser reports were tagged hint, and 15 hint reports were tagged parser. The browser locale and intake tag do not establish the tenant's configuration.

5 reports describe a one-day move, but remain counted under parser by the kb's tenant/channel rule: R-41202, R-41209, R-41236, R-41344, R-41620. This description alone does not prove a timezone or DST defect; do not invent a third cause or count these reports twice. Preserve their wording for verification during the fix.

The table’s ticket column records the export’s state before this split: the hint cause had no ticket of its own then. Both causes now have the GitHub tickets linked above.

Counts come from uniqueById, groupByCause and readAs in src/lib/kb/causes.ts, using the exported tenant directory through tenantOf. They are calculated when this page renders, not copied from intake labels or typed into this page.

Two fixes, two tickets
Shared parser

Track the parser cause in GitHub issue 1. For a day-first tenant, the shared parser reads the month before the day. Report R-41200 describes 7 April becoming 4 July for Harbour Dental (en-GB, app). Report R-41205 is also a parser report despite its intake hint tag and en-US browser locale: Morrow Tax’s tenant locale is fr-FR.

The fix must respect the tenant’s intended date format through the shared parsing path. Test ambiguous dates in both directions, unambiguous days above 12, and every affected channel. Retain the one-day descriptions as regression evidence without claiming an unproved separate defect.

Booking-v3 field hint

Track the hint cause in GitHub issue 2. For day-first tenants on booking-v3, the field says MM/DD/YYYY while the form reads dates day-first. People follow that hint and the form interprets their input in the opposite order. Report R-41230 is Copper Studio’s booking-v3 form (es-ES), even though intake tagged it parser. R-41241 is the same cause for Alder Physio (de-DE); the browser locale does not change the tenant.

Align the visible hint and form validation with the tenant’s date format. Test booking-v3 for Alder Physio, Copper Studio and Pale Harbour, and ensure booking-v2 remains correct. Fixing the shared parser alone does not fix this misleading instruction.

The queue is not the incident clock

Read received and merged timestamps separately. Parser reports begin on 1 April; hint reports begin on 17 April. The large merge spike in the week of 29 June is backlog processing, not the first occurrence or a surge in newly received reports. Reports continue after that merge, through the export’s last received date in October. Neither a merge nor the word “known” proves a fix shipped.

How the desk handles the next report
Deduplicate export rows by report ID. Read the subject and body, then look up the product, tenant locale, booking form version and channel; browser locale and intake tags are only clues.
For this booking system, use the tenant-aware cause rule in causes.ts: a day-first tenant on a booking-v3 form belongs to the hint cause; other affected paths belong to parser.
Merge only when the cause and fix match an existing ticket. Different subjects can share a cause; identical subjects can hide different causes. A missing tenant or unplaced cause needs investigation, not a subject-only merge. Never default to merging when unsure.
Keep one ticket per confirmed cause and keep its report count and evidence current. When new reports arrive, add their data, rerun the analysis and render, then update the matching ticket. Do not close a newly different problem as a duplicate of #4471 just because it mentions a date.
Require evidence that the relevant fix shipped and that its regression tests pass before marking it fixed. A known status or queued fix does not stop the desk from triaging continuing reports.

The live cases show why subject matching fails: different subjects and channels can share a cause; the same subject and tenant can differ by channel; identical subjects with no tenant establish no cause.

Maintenance and provenance

Owner: md-400, with GPT-6.1 Sol as the writing and analysis harness. Evidence: the supplied support kb export, its original classifier, tenant directory, report data, desk notes, and the rendered tables above. The export is a snapshot, not a live service. The desk should compare later reports with current product evidence rather than assume this snapshot never changes.

Rebuild the page after data or rule changes. Preserve accepted decisions and add a new numbered record when policy changes again. The rendered desk reference below is computed from this page’s signature by the supplied RenderStamp component; it is not a hand-written identifier.
